summary: This regulation explains the rules for companies that have listed non-convertible debt securities or redeemable preference shares and want to do a scheme of arrangement. Such a company must first get a No-objection letter from the stock exchange before filing the scheme with the National Company Law Tribunal. It must also share certain documents with the stock exchange after the Tribunal approves the scheme.
points: Must file the draft scheme of arrangement with the stock exchange along with a non-refundable fee to get a No-objection letter before filing with the National Company Law Tribunal.
Must not file any scheme of arrangement with the National Company Law Tribunal without first getting a No-objection letter from the stock exchange.
Must place the stock exchange's No-objection letter before the National Company Law Tribunal when seeking approval for the scheme.
Must file the draft scheme with the National Company Law Tribunal within six months of the stock exchange issuing the No-objection letter.
Must submit specific documents to the stock exchange after the National Company Law Tribunal sanctions the scheme.
Must follow any other requirements set by the Board from time to time.
example: Sunrise Steel Private Limited has listed its non-convertible debt securities on a recognized stock exchange and plans to undertake a scheme of arrangement under the Companies Act, 2013. Before filing this scheme with the National Company Law Tribunal, Sunrise Steel Private Limited files the draft scheme and a non-refundable fee with the stock exchange to obtain a No-objection letter. Once the letter is issued, the company ensures it files the draft scheme with the Tribunal within six months while presenting the No-objection letter during the approval process. After the Tribunal sanctions the scheme, Sunrise Steel Private Limited submits all required documents to the stock exchange.

terms.meaning: A court-approved plan between a company and its creditors or shareholders, such as a merger or restructuring.
A quasi-judicial body in India that handles corporate disputes and company law matters.

watch: People often forget that the No-objection letter from the stock exchange must be used to file the scheme with the Tribunal within six months of its issuance.
